deprecations_pending.description:
The `aggregate` transform now also emits the failed-updates counter with the `_total` suffix, matching Vector's counter naming convention:

- `aggregate_failed_updates_total`

The previous name without the `_total` suffix is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Migrate any dashboards or alerts that reference:

- `aggregate_failed_updates`

deprecations_pending.what: Boolean shorthand for object-valued configuration options
deprecations_pending.description:
Boolean shorthand for object-valued configuration options is deprecated. Use the object form instead
so that each setting has one consistent representation and the options being configured are explicit.

Existing boolean values continue to work. Removal is not yet scheduled. We will give users at least
one month to migrate before removing this shorthand.

This applies to `healthcheck` on sinks, global and sink `acknowledgements`, `jetstream` on the NATS sink,
and `acknowledgements` on the Splunk HEC source.
Ordinary boolean options, such as `healthcheck.enabled`, are unaffected.

Please also see the [dedicated note for `use_otlp_decoding`](/deprecations/#opentelemetry-use_otlp_decoding).

### Settings with an `enabled` field

For `healthcheck`, global and sink `acknowledgements`, NATS sink `jetstream`, and Splunk HEC source
`acknowledgements`, replace the boolean with an object containing the same value in `enabled`.
For example, within a sink configuration, replace:

```yaml
healthcheck: false
acknowledgements: true
```

with:

```yaml
healthcheck:
  enabled: false
acknowledgements:
  enabled: true
```

Other options in these objects retain their defaults. Use the same transformation for either `true`
or `false`.

deprecations_pending.what: legacy memory enrichment table counters without the `_total` suffix
deprecations_pending.description:
The memory enrichment table failure and TTL-expiration counters are now also emitted with the
`_total` suffix, matching Vector's counter naming convention:

- `memory_enrichment_table_failed_insertions_total`
- `memory_enrichment_table_failed_reads_total`
- `memory_enrichment_table_ttl_expirations_total`

The previous names without the `_total` suffix are deprecated and will be removed in a future
release. Migrate any dashboards or alerts that reference:

- `memory_enrichment_table_failed_insertions`
- `memory_enrichment_table_failed_reads`
- `memory_enrichment_table_ttl_expirations`

The `opentelemetry` source's `use_otlp_decoding` option is deprecated. Switch to `decoding` with `codec: otlp` to preserve the same behavior as `use_otlp_decoding: true`. To preserve the OTLP representation of all signals, replace: ```yaml use_otlp_decoding: true ``` with: ```yaml decoding: codec: otlp ``` To preserve OTLP only for selected signals, replace: ```yaml use_otlp_decoding: logs: false metrics: false traces: true ``` with: ```yaml decoding: codec: otlp signal_types: ["traces"] ``` Existing boolean and object settings still work, but produce a deprecation warning. When migrating: - Leave out `signal_types` to keep all signals in OTLP format. Any types not included will remain in Vector's native format. - If you currently use `use_otlp_decoding: false`, remove it and leave out `decoding`. Native conversion remains the default. - Use `codec: otlp` and the signal names `logs`, `metrics`, and `traces`. Other values are not supported. - Remove `use_otlp_decoding` when adding `decoding`. Setting both prevents Vector from starting.

Stable Vector release archives and packages are now hosted in the public COSE
release bucket. The `packages.timber.io/vector` URLs are deprecated and users should
switch to `install.datadoghq.com/vector` instead.

Starting with Vector `0.59.0`, the Vector installer and the download
instructions on [vector.dev](https://vector.dev/download/) point to artifacts
in the COSE bucket. Existing `packages.timber.io` URLs continue to work during
the deprecation period.

| Artifact | Migration outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Stable Vector releases, installers, and package-manager downloads | Migrated to exact-version paths under `install.datadoghq.com/vector/<version>/`; stable `latest` or `.X` aliases are not provided |
| `packages.timber.io/vector` versioned, `latest`, and version-alias URLs | Remain readable through December 31, 2026, and may be deleted at any time after that date |
| Nightly and custom builds | Treated as transient artifacts that are superseded by stable releases, so existing builds are not migrated; future builds are published to `install.datadoghq.com` under `vector/nightly/` and `vector/custom/` |
| Helm charts | [GitHub Release assets](https://github.com/vectordotdev/helm-charts/releases); `https://helm.vector.dev` remains the Helm repository index |
| All other legacy artifacts | Not migrated and will be deleted |

The `host_metrics` source now also emits the process runtime counter with the `_total` suffix, matching Vector's counter naming convention:

- `process_runtime_total`

The previous name without the `_total` suffix is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Migrate any dashboards or alerts that reference:

- `process_runtime`

deprecations_enacted.what: GreptimeDB v0.x support in `greptimedb_metrics` and `greptimedb_logs` sinks
deprecations_enacted.description:
The `greptimedb_metrics` and `greptimedb_logs` sinks drop support for GreptimeDB v0.x.
Users must upgrade their GreptimeDB instance to v1.x before upgrading Vector.
The `encoding` field will be removed. Use `decoding` and `framing` instead.

The `buffer_byte_size` and `buffer_events` gauges are deprecated in favor of the
`buffer_size_bytes` and `buffer_size_events` metrics.

The `azure_monitor_logs` sink is deprecated in favor of the new `azure_logs_ingestion` sink,
which uses the Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API.

Users should migrate before Microsoft ends support for the old Data Collector API (scheduled
for September 2026).

deprecations_enacted.what: Boolean syntax for the `compression` field in the `vector` sink
deprecations_enacted.description:
The boolean syntax (`compression: true` / `compression: false`) is deprecated.
Use the string syntax instead: `compression: "gzip"`, `compression: "zstd"`, or `compression: "none"`.

The `bool_or_vector_compression` deserializer will be removed once the boolean syntax is no longer supported.

The `series_api_version: v1` option is deprecated in favor of `v2` (the default).
The v1 series endpoint (`/api/v1/series`) is a legacy endpoint.

Users should remove `series_api_version: v1` from their configuration or set it to `v2`.

deprecations_enacted.what: omitting the `version` field on `influxdb_logs` and `influxdb_metrics` sinks
deprecations_enacted.description:
The `version` field selects the InfluxDB API version whose settings are used. It will be required
in a future release. Until then, when `version` is unset the version is inferred from the
configured settings.

- `version: "1"` uses the v1 settings: `database`, `consistency`, `retention_policy_name`,
  `username`, and `password`.
- `version: "2"` uses the v2 settings: `org`, `bucket`, and `token`.

Migrate by adding `version: "1"` or `version: "2"` to match the settings already present:

```yaml
sinks:
  my_sink:
    type: influxdb_logs
    version: "2"
    org: my-org
    bucket: vector-bucket
    token: ${INFLUXDB_TOKEN}
```

deprecations_enacted.what: Environment-variable and secret placeholders in non-string positions
deprecations_enacted.description:
Vector now parses configuration files before substituting environment variables and
`SECRET[backend.key]` references. Only string values are substituted, then converted
to the field's declared type. Substituted values cannot add configuration structure.

Configuration must be valid before substitution. Quote placeholders in TOML and JSON,
including numeric and boolean fields. In YAML flow collections, use quoted placeholders,
such as `inputs: ["${SOURCE}"]`. The same quoting rules apply to secret references.

Use literal map keys, component names, and table headers. Replace placeholders that
expanded into multiple array elements with an explicit list of individual values.
Remove escaping that was needed only for the outer configuration format; escaping
required by an embedded language such as VRL is still necessary.

See the [environment-variable migration guidance](/docs/reference/environment_variables/#security-restrictions)
and [secret configuration documentation](/docs/reference/configuration/secrets/) for details.

deprecations_enacted.what: scheme-less `address` and `routing.endpoints` values in the `vector` sink defaulting to `http`
deprecations_enacted.description:
A `vector` sink endpoint such as `127.0.0.1` without an explicit scheme currently defaults to `http`.
This behavior is deprecated and will change to `https` in a future release.
Note that when TLS is enabled, a scheme-less address already defaults to `https`.

Migrate by specifying the scheme explicitly:

```yaml
sinks:
  my_sink:
    type: vector
    address: http://127.0.0.1:6000
```
